newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mixed on confused outlook.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mixed on confused outlook.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mixed on Wednesday on different opinions about the future market trend, traders said.

The most active June 1997 contract ended at 23,600 yuan ($2,845) per tonne, unchanged from Tuesday's close. It opened at 23,550 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 23,660 and a low of 23,500 yuan per tonne.
March fell 30 to 23,150, April rose 40 to 23,390, May dropped 50 to 23,550, July decreased 20 to 23,580 and August was up 110 to 23,950.
Combined volume rose to 56,040 tonnes from 36,900.
Copper opened little changed and moved in a narrow range for most of the session with investors mixed about the direction it will take after consolidations in the past few sessions, traders said.
"Many investors do not know what to do in the current situation," one trader said.
"The rises in combined volume indicate copper is likely to fluctuate in a wide range in the next few days," he added.
Traders said Shanghai copper appears to have lost any clear direction and the lack of market-moving news made it better to stay on the sidelines.
Aluminium ended up across the board. March rose 180 to 15,980 yuan per tonne, April 190 to 16,370, May 250 to 16,700 and June 250 to 16,950.
Combined volume rose to 6,280 tonnes from 2,750.
